Package io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava

Record Class TopicInfo

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.mdudel.zenoh.purejava.TopicInfo
Record Components:
keyExpr - the fully resolved key expression, with any router keyexpr alias already expanded
sources - every observation channel that has seen this topic; never empty, and see TopicSource for what each one does and does not prove
activeSources - the subset of sources whose evidence still stands. Empty means the topic was seen earlier in the run and has since gone away
firstSeenMs - wall-clock time this topic was first seen, in milliseconds since the epoch
lastSeenMs - wall-clock time of the most recent positive evidence, in milliseconds since the epoch. A withdrawal does not advance it, so on an inactive topic this is when it was last actually there
sampleCount - how many messages were actually observed on this key. Zero when the topic is known only from declarations, which is the common case for a topic nobody published to during the window
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<TopicInfo>
public record TopicInfo(String keyExpr, Set<TopicSource> sources, Set<TopicSource> activeSources, long firstSeenMs, long lastSeenMs, long sampleCount) extends Record implements Comparable<TopicInfo>
One discovered topic, as reported by TopicRegistry.snapshot().

An immutable point-in-time view. Taking a second snapshot produces fresh instances rather than mutating these, so a snapshot can be held, sorted, or serialised without worrying about the registry changing underneath it.

Ever seen versus still there

sources() is cumulative and never shrinks: it is every channel that has observed this topic since the registry picked it up. activeSources() is the subset whose evidence is still standing right now. The two differ once a declaration is withdrawn, which only becomes visible in a cumulative registry, because a live one drops the entry outright. See TopicRegistry for that distinction.

    • active

      public boolean active()
      True if any evidence for this topic still stands.

      Equivalently: true if a live (non-cumulative) registry would still be reporting this topic. False only happens in a cumulative registry, and means every declaration has been withdrawn and no message was ever observed on the key.

    • hasTraffic

      public boolean hasTraffic()
      True if a message was actually observed on this key.

    • isDeclarationOnly

      public boolean isDeclarationOnly()
      True if this topic is known only because something declared an interest in it, with no message ever observed. Useful for telling "a subscriber is waiting here" apart from "data is flowing here".
